# DCH round 4 guard-removal table

**6,100 guard entries / 10,584 negative cases / 11,249 total direct cases.** Every guard has a flipping negative. Zero mandatory negatives are masked; zero guards lack witnesses; zero mutation exceptions count as rejection. Native execution is NOT_RUN.

The declaration inventory covers all **7,031 original primitive constraints in 34 owned schemas**, grouped into **5,998 logical schema guards**, plus the function and preflight guards. The independent `Plans/dch_schema_guard_fixtures.json` freezes source rule values and 4,923 one-change witnesses. Default verification never reconstructs its negatives from changed schema definitions. It refuses missing/changed rules, unsupported validation vocabulary and missing witnesses. Explicit fixture rebuilding is a review operation, never a regression bypass.

Source rule correspondence and input hashes are retained in `declared-schema-rule-map.json` under the round-4 evidence directory. Selector parameters inside if/not are recorded separately; their enclosing branch/negation owns validation. Nullable primitive alternatives use an equivalent union type with type-specific constraints. Required, distinct schema_id constants make the object editions disjoint, so their oneOf/anyOf forms accept the same unmutated set. The root-object guard includes object assurance otherwise duplicated by the dispatcher. Required fixed edition tags include unreachable opposite-edition scope copies. All these logical copies are identified as one rule; unrelated guards remain enforced.

The negative IDs resolve in `DCH-guard-negative-index.json`. U denotes its complete exact ID set, `N0001` through `N10584`. The rejected-set column gives an exact complement, not a sample. Every mutation is in memory; guards are restored per row.

Function variants replace the real checker AST predicate with its accepting value. Schema variants suppress the exact normalized document/path keyword (required members separately). Equivalent copies also include closed-payload definitions, identifier pattern/length/format, archive constants/predecessors, terminal code/kind/evidence, and checkpoint consumer/projector joins. Scope canonicalization is one CV-365 relation; retry fields are removed from every comparison and preserve observational actor copies. Missing-body/generation controls deliberately inject fail-open behavior only in their missing-source branch; production has no fallback.

All original fixture negatives remain mandatory. Candidate exploration retains only isolated witnesses, then freezes them; default checks require every frozen witness. Pure-schema conjunction/alternative rejection certificates reuse a rejection only while an unchanged blocking rule remains in every possible admitting branch. Other unreached pure guards reuse the deterministic baseline. Every potentially accepting removal is reevaluated. This avoids replaying unrelated negatives without hiding a possible acceptance.
